document.title: Phase 6: Platform bindings
document.p: Goal (PLAN.md): Kotlin and Swift bindings, Android and iOS builds, and binding tests on device in CI. Design: . The bindings mirror the JavaScript package (, , ): the same concepts, the same defaults, the same errors, in each language's own idiom. Rules for parallel packets are those of docs/tasks/phase-2.md (, , : a packet starts when every packet in its "After" list is committed). Phase 6 changes no public header and must not regress any count of Phases 2 to 7.

item.p: One host shim, three hosts. The C layer under the JavaScript package (bindings/javascript/sxml_javascript*.c, , ) already turns the public API into what a garbage-collected or reference-counted host needs: handles, flat request structs, one error record per processor, side results (), JSON-shaped input through fn:parse-json, and serialization into a processor-owned output. It builds natively in every preset. Packet moves it to bindings/host/ as the host shim (glossary , header bindings/host/sxml_host.h, not a public header) with the resolver as an interface instead of a WebAssembly import. Then:
JavaScript: sxml.wasm and sxml-full.wasm link the host shim and a thin export file. The export names stay sxml_javascript_*, so src/index.ts does not change.
Kotlin: a JNI glue file (glossary ) turns Kotlin request objects into host shim requests. Nothing else is in C.
Swift: the Swift package imports the host shim through a module map (CSxmlHost) and calls it directly. There is no Swift-specific C.
No binding reimplements value conversion, side results or error copying. A fix in the shim fixes all three.

The same API in three languages (below): a Processor (resolver, optional features), parse, compile once and evaluate many times, value from host data by the fn:parse-json rule, serialize with fn:serialize's options, XQuery (compileQuery), XSLT (compileStylesheet), XSD (compileSchema), side results delivered after the call, errors with status, code, description, source name, line and column, and the DUCET shipped beside the library.

Kotlin: every object that owns C memory is AutoCloseable (use {}). A java.lang.ref.Cleaner releases what is never closed, as the JavaScript package's FinalizationRegistry does. Objects made by a processor hold it strongly, so it is not collected while they live. Closing a processor closes everything it made.
Swift: ARC. deinit releases, and objects retain their processor, so the order is always right. There is no close().
Threads (: a processor is used by one thread at a time).
Kotlin: every call on a processor or its objects holds the processor's lock, Cleaner actions included. Separate processors run in parallel.
Swift: Processor and its objects are not Sendable. Strict concurrency (Swift 6 language mode) rejects sharing them across isolation domains at compile time.

Callbacks never recurse into the same processor (). The resolver is the only callback that runs during a call. As in JavaScript, it must not use its own processor: the binding throws (Kotlin IllegalStateException, Swift SxmlUsageError). An exception it throws is kept by the binding, the shim stops with SXML_STATUS_INPUT_OUTPUT_FAILED, and the call rethrows the same exception. Messages, updated trees and result documents are side results, given to the host's callbacks after the call ().
Text crosses as UTF-8 bytes. Kotlin passes ByteArrays (encodeToByteArray), never jstring. JNI's "modified UTF-8" encodes U+0000 and supplementary characters differently. Swift passes String.utf8.
One library per platform, with every language and every optional feature except EXPath File (as sxml-full.wasm):
Android and JVM: libsxml_kotlin.so, which is the library, the host shim and the JNI glue, statically linked. Only the JNI entry points are exported.
Apple: Sxml.xcframework, a static library of the library and the host shim, for iOS devices, iOS simulators and macOS.
Linux, for Swift: the CMake target sxml_host.
A core-only native variant ('s other link) is not planned. A packet adds one when a host asks for it.

Nothing changes in the C library but two Android fallbacks (6.3). Bionic declares aligned_alloc only from API 28 and timespec_get from API 29. The library is C17 and compiles with -Werror for all four ABIs at API 29 as it is (6.1 probe). For minSdk 24 (the default taken, ), src/allocator.c uses posix_memalign and src/processor.c uses clock_gettime when __ANDROID_API__ is lower. Each is one branch beside the existing _WIN32 one.

section.title: The binding APIs ()
section.p: The same names as the JavaScript package unless the language has its own idiom. Options are named arguments with defaults, not option objects.

section.title: Kotlin (bindings/kotlin, package dev.tinyactors.sxml)

item.p: Sxml.version, Sxml.features (the library's optional features, by name).

Processor(resolver: Resolver? = null, features: Set<String>? = null, collationData: CollationData = CollationData.Bundled). features = null means all; an unknown name is IllegalArgumentException. CollationData.None turns the shipped DUCET off, and CollationData.Bytes(ByteArray) supplies another one. The library loads with the class (System.loadLibrary("sxml_kotlin")). There is no load(), because the module is not fetched as a WebAssembly file is.

parse(xml: String | ByteArray, uri: String? = null): Value; compile(expression, variables: List<String> = emptyList(), namespaces: Map<String, String> = emptyMap(), baseUri: String? = null): XPathExpression, whose evaluate(context: Any? = null, variables: Map<String, Any?> = emptyMap()) returns a Value; evaluate(expression, ...) compiles and evaluates once; value(data: Any?); serialize(value, options).

Input (Any?): a Value of this processor, a String (an xs:string), or JSON-shaped data that fn:parse-json reads: Number, Boolean, null (the empty sequence), List<*>, Array<*> and Map<String, *>. Anything else is IllegalArgumentException. This is the one rule of .
Value : AutoCloseable: toString() (adaptive), serialize(options: Map<String, Any?> = emptyMap()), whose keys may be camelCase.

XQuery: compileQuery(text, namespaces, baseUri): XQuery, with evaluate(context, variables, updates: UpdateSink? = null, messages: ((Message) -> Unit)? = null), serialize(value), run(...) and isUpdating. UpdateSink has updatedTree(UpdatedTree) and putDocument(PutDocument) with defaults; without a putDocument, fn:put raises FOUP0002 ().

XSLT: compileStylesheet(text, baseUri, staticParameters): Stylesheet, with transform(source, initialMatchSelection, initialMode, initialTemplate, initialFunction, args, parameters, templateParameters, tunnelParameters, baseOutputUri, delivery: ResultDelivery = SERIALIZED, resultDocumentDelivery, serialization, messages): TransformResult (output, value, resultDocuments). InitialMode.Unnamed selects the unnamed mode.

XSD: compileSchema(documents: List<SchemaDocument>, baseUri): Schema, where SchemaDocument is Text(text, uri) or Resolved(uri), with validate(input: Value | String | ByteArray, mode, type, uri): ValidationResult (validity: Validity, reports, document).

fun interface Resolver { fun resolve(request: ResourceRequest): Resource? }. ResourceRequest(kind: ResourceKind, uriReference, absoluteUri). Resource.Text(String) or Resource.Bytes(ByteArray). ResourceKind is an enum of the 13 kinds of the JavaScript package, XML_DOCUMENT to LOCALE_DATA.

Errors: open class SxmlException(status: Status, code: String, codeNamespaceUri, codeLocalName, description, sourceName, lineNumber, columnNumber) : Exception; class SchemaException(..., reports: List<SchemaReport>). Status is an enum of sxml_status's names. A failed allocation is SxmlException(OUT_OF_MEMORY), not OutOfMemoryError.

Memory: Processor, XPathExpression, XQuery, Stylesheet, Schema and Value are AutoCloseable, and close() is idempotent. Using an object after it is closed is IllegalStateException. The values a call gives you (results, updated trees, result documents) are yours to close. Processor.liveAllocationCount() is for tests.

section.title: Swift (bindings/swift, module Sxml; Package.swift at the repository root)

item.p: Sxml.version, Sxml.features.

Processor(resolver: Resolver? = nil, features: Set<String>? = nil, collationData: CollationData = .bundled) throws. typealias Resolver = (ResourceRequest) throws -> Resource?. enum Resource { case text(String), bytes([UInt8]) }. enum ResourceKind: String uses the JavaScript names ("xml-document", ...).
parse(_ xml: String | [UInt8], uri:), compile(_:variables:namespaces: baseURI:), XPathExpression.evaluate(context:variables:), evaluate(_:...), value(_:), serialize(_:options:).
Input: protocol XdmInput. Value, String, Bool, Int, Double, [XdmInput?], [String: XdmInput?] and nil (the empty sequence) conform, with the same fn:parse-json rule.

XQuery, XSLT and XSD as in Kotlin, with Swift argument labels (compileQuery(_:namespaces:baseURI:), query.evaluate(context:variables:updates:messages:), stylesheet.transform(source:...), compileSchema(_:baseURI:).validate(_:mode:type:uri:)). UpdateSink is a struct of two optional closures.

Errors: struct SxmlError: Error, CustomStringConvertible (status: Status, code, codeNamespaceURI, codeLocalName, description, sourceName, lineNumber, columnNumber); struct SchemaError: Error (error, reports); enum SxmlUsageError: Error for misuse (a resolver that uses its processor, a value of another processor). The calls use untyped throws, because a resolver's own error is rethrown as it is.

Memory: final classes under ARC. Objects retain their processor. A resolver must not capture its processor strongly (a cycle), and it may not use it anyway. The DUCET is a SwiftPM resource (Bundle.module).

Parity by name: every binding has the tests of the JavaScript package's test/package.test.ts and test/full.test.ts, with the same names, the same inputs and the same expected text, plus tests of its own ownership rules (close and Cleaner in Kotlin, ARC in Swift, threads). 6.12 compares the three lists.

Leaks and allocation failures (), as the JavaScript tests do: every test ends with the processor's live allocation count 0, and one test runs the allocation-failure loop through failingAllocationNumber.
ctest, so the usual gates see the bindings:

kotlin/jvm: the JNI glue built for the host. The tests are compiled by kotlinc (SXML_KOTLINC, or kotlinc on PATH) with kotlin.test and a small main runner, so ctest needs no Gradle and no network. It is skipped when kotlinc or JNI is not found.
swift/linux: swift build and swift test against sxml_host from the same build tree. It is skipped without swift.
android/build: under an Android preset, the four ABIs build with -Werror and their unit tests compile. A size report is printed.
On devices (owner or CI):
Android instrumented tests: the same Kotlin test sources as an androidTest source set. They run on an x86_64 emulator at API 24 and API 35, and on one arm64 device.
Swift: xcodebuild test on an iOS simulator and one iOS device; swift test on macOS.
